I'm being asked why the US broke a decade-plus policy of not interfering with the market-setting of exchange rates.
I suspect the drivers include:
Trade Competitiveness: Washington sees an excessively weak yen as a drag on American trade competitiveness, not just in bilateral trade with Japan but also in third markets across the globe.
Yield Concerns: In past solo interventions, Tokyo has tended to fund its yen purchases by selling US Treasuries, a move that inadvertently pushes bond yields higher and drives up domestic borrowing costs for the American government, companies, and households.
The upside for both countries is clear: This type of joint intervention carries a lot more weight, and markets are paying attention, at least initially.
The catch for the US? Washington has now signed onto a strategy whose ultimate success doesn't rest in its own hands. Instead, as discussed in previous posts, it hinges on a comprehensive policy alignment in Tokyo among the Bank of Japan, the Ministry of Finance, and the Prime Minister’s Office.
#economy #markets #japan #yen #currency #intervention #fx

The GPT-Pro models should be thrown out of this set, because it's been reported that the Pro series is a best-of-10 rollout on the same commercially available base model. July was a quiet month at the index level.

Underneath the surface, it was one of the most violent hedge fund and factor unwinds in decades.

Crowded AI trades collapsed. Momentum was crushed. Margin calls hit. A major portfolio was forced into the market.

Based on history, this was a cleansing event.

But the bigger story is the disruption AI is causing:

• Market structure has changed forever
• Factor volatility is structurally higher
• AI is compressing economic time
• Terminal values are becoming harder to estimate
• Leverage is turning valuation uncertainty into liquidity risk
• Compute demand remains insatiable

The S&P is still in a bull market. Earnings remain strong. Breadth is healthy. The AI trade has corrected in both price and time.

Now the question is whether we get a true follow-through day pattern confirming that the panic low was a durable bottom for AI trades.

The reason I don’t tell anyone to go all in bitcoin or any single asset and to own other assets (at least 3 )is not from a lack of belief or understanding 

It’s because precisely for the fact as we have seen that each asset - depending on its qualities has different downsides and upsides  

Ie you may own property in a country that ends up in a war or earthquake even if fundamentals are great - you could own something and it gets confiscated by the government or taxed and regulated to death or lose from loss of trust in the currency

Similarly the number 1 reason for not being all in btc is the agency component - you could be right and still lose due to losing wallet/keys etc

Every asset has its upside and downside - In Bitcoin the downside is in wallet control which is why the thesis is the improvement in infrastructure to better support and mitigate it over time aswell 

As we saw even the biggest technical  advocates have blind spots 

You must acknowledge to yourself that no matter how much you think you know there is always a blind spot 

We can’t mitigate all things but consciously going through different scenarios upfront will help 

I’m concerned with the trend of these all in one stock etc traders aswell as they preach “it’s only if you don’t know what you are doing” 

The problem is because you “know” what you are doing that you lose - the inability to see how you could get slaughtered

My general view on hardware wallets is the same as exchanges 

Generally using the largest and well known is better than obscure 

1)if there is a hack on a smaller brand you are on your own with very little resources - if you use a big brand and there is a wide hack there is immense resources to both increase awareness, recover and find culprits aswell as incentive to refund losses 

2)if a large provider suffers a massive hack the whole space is screwed for a while anyway being on an obscure wallet wasn’t going to save you from downside in price 

3) psychologically it’s easier to deal with loss when everyone is on same boat 

4)if an industry wide drop happens like ftx style prices get so low that even if you lost from the major hack just investing a fraction from elsewhere can recreate your position if it’s a temporary issue 

There are so many considerations outside of just security in a technical sense 

These are just some things to consider
